Obstreperous

/uhb-STREP-er-uhs/ - the stress falls on STREP · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Obstreperous means noisy and difficult to control.

The obstreperous freshman section drummed the bleachers through both anthems and every whistle.

Worked Example

Halfway through the estate auction, the back row turned obstreperous—bidding by air horn, shouting over the auctioneer's patter, rattling the folding chairs—until the gavel came down and the lot was withdrawn entirely.

Obstreperous adds defiance to volume: a loud room is merely noisy, but an obstreperous one is noisy against whoever is trying to run it—it resists being brought to order.

How Obstreperous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rowdy

rowdy: loud and rough, usually in fun; obstreperous adds active resistance to control

unruly

unruly: refusing to be governed; obstreperous does it at full volume

Antonyms

meek

meek: quietly submissive, giving no trouble at all

quiet

quiet: simply making little noise

How Strong Is It? — fidgety → rowdy → obstreperous

fidgety vs. obstreperous

fidgety vs. obstreperous: Fidgety stops far short of obstreperous — fidgeting is squirmy motion, not defiance of the room.

rowdy vs. obstreperous

rowdy vs. obstreperous: Rowdy stops short of obstreperous — a rowdy crowd is loud in fun, while an obstreperous one is loud against control.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of obstreperous.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ob-

Prefix — ob-: against, in the way

Root — streper-

Root — streper-: to make a racket (Latin strepere)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Ob- (against) + streper- (to make a racket) + -ous = full of noise made against someone. Latin strepere was the roar of a crowd; point that roar against whoever holds the gavel and you have obstreperous — noise as resistance.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: The heart of this word is Latin strepere, 'to make a racket' — a wonderfully noisy verb that left no other descendants in everyday English. You may recognize the prefix ob- ('against') from words like object, but the racket in obstreperous is all its own; learn the word whole.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / often humorous

Obstreperous suits crowds, children, and animals who are loud and fighting control — often with a raised eyebrow of humor. Plain 'rowdy' covers cheerful noise; reserve obstreperous for noise aimed at whoever is trying to restore order. Its unit-mate querulous is the opposite volume of trouble: a stream of whiny complaints rather than a roar.
